title: How long does PFG-03M and VRP-M last?

posts.topic_title: How long does PFG-03M and VRP-M last?
posts.author: eric343
posts.post_subject: How long does PFG-03M and VRP-M last?
posts.content_md:
I opened a refrigerator right outside the holography lab, and discovered a pile of Slavich media left over from Steven Benton and the Spatial Imaging Group -- everything from 4x5 to 8x10 AND BIGGER!

Up until now we've been using the lab's old stock of Agfa media (boxes and boxes!), but it would be interesting to play around... (especially since nobody would likely mind my using the Slavich stuff for experiments)

Unfortunately, all the dates are 1997/1998. Is there any hope for these boxes?

I think I also saw some old BB panchromatic and Ultimate plates kicking around somewhere. How do those age?

posts.content_md:
> **eric343:** I opened a refrigerator right outside the holography lab, and discovered a pile of Slavich media left over from Steven Benton and the Spatial Imaging Group -- everything from 4x5 to 8x10 AND BIGGER!Up until now we've been using the lab's old stock of Agfa media (boxes and boxes!), but it would be interesting to play around... (especially since nobody would likely mind my using the Slavich stuff for experiments)Unfortunately, all the dates are 1997/1998. Is there any hope for these boxes?I think I also saw some old BB panchromatic and Ultimate plates kicking around somewhere. How do those age?

I have successfully killed bad fogging on Slavich plates (without also killing the photosensitivity) by soaking them for exactly 60 seconds in a solution of; 

20g Ferric EDTA and 10 g KBr per litre. (This solution keeps for years.) 

(Ferric EDTA is ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid ferric sodium salt)

What amazed me was that the photosensitivity of the plates did not drop noticeably afterwards without my needing to resensitise them in say 2% ascorbic acid (vitamin C) at pH ~6.

BB plates:

I often use BB plates which are now in their 9th year without doing more than giving them the TEA solution treatment which I would do normally anyway. They are then as good as new.

Jeff
